status.label: Compare non-secure UAC focus
status.detail: Maintainers reproduced the failure; similar taskbar behavior leaves Windows versus Run ownership unresolved.

next_action.label: Trace foreground handoff on elevation
next_action.reason: Use the existing recordings and explicit UAC setting rather than asking the reporter to supply them again.

judgment.rationale: A maintainer reproduced the non-dimming UAC focus problem and a later Windows 11 reproduction exists. Comments also report the same behavior from the taskbar, so a PowerToys-specific root cause is not established.
evidence: The report gives Run activation, application selection and Ctrl+Shift+Enter steps with non-dimming UAC.
https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/4933#issuecomment-2194494049 confirms Windows 11 reproduction; other comments report taskbar/OS behavior too.
judgment.recommended_action: Compare Run, Start and taskbar elevation under the same UAC policy; measure focus and hide ordering before deciding ownership.

fix_assessment.rationale: A Run-specific foreground-handoff correction is a conditional candidate. An equivalent Windows failure would instead require OS escalation; no linked concrete PowerToys fix was found in the inspected timeline.

proposed_fixes.title: Validate and correct Run's elevation focus handoff
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: Run's activation/hide ordering retains or reacquires foreground focus while a non-secure-desktop UAC consent window is being created. Equivalent taskbar failures are counterevidence and may indicate Windows ownership.
plan: On a disposable test machine, record Run visibility/foreground changes around elevation and compare Start/taskbar launch with exactly the same UAC setting and target executable.

Trace the selected result's elevation delegate and launcher hide/focus-restoration ordering in src/modules/launcher. Determine whether Run performs a late foreground restoration after the consent window appears.
Only if a Run-specific ordering defect is proven, remove or defer that restoration and complete the normal hide transition before elevation. Do not manipulate consent UI, bypass UAC or weaken policy.

Add an integration case for cancellation and successful elevation; if all entry points share the failure, attach the focused reproduction to Windows ownership rather than shipping a focus-stealing workaround.
verification: With non-dimming UAC, keyboard navigation reaches the consent decision without Alt+Tab when the platform allows it.
Secure-desktop UAC, cancelled elevation, ordinary launches and Run reactivation preserve normal focus and security behavior.

confidence.rationale: The behavior is reproduced, but comparable OS/taskbar symptoms prevent attributing the cause to Run.

issue_context.summary: Run elevation can show a UAC consent dialog without moving keyboard focus to it when desktop dimming is disabled; this has been reproduced on Windows 10 and 11.
known_information: The author supplied a second recording explaining expected versus actual focus.
A maintainer reproduced the specific non-dimming setting.
The author's early text conflates 'Never notify' with 'do not dim'; the later maintainer reproduction identifies the meaningful non-dimming configuration.
Other contributors describe similar behavior outside PowerToys; the issue remains open and unassigned.
inferences: Run may have a focus-handoff race, but the OS may own the common failure.
Non-dimming UAC must not be confused with disabling consent entirely.
issue_context.analysis: The report is sufficiently detailed for controlled maintainer reproduction. Neither 'by design' nor 'PowerToys defect' is established by opinion in the discussion.
initial_investigation: Read all ten comments and both recordings' accompanying explanations.
Inspected timeline cross-references: a gsudo issue and a later duplicate-like report describe the same family, not a covering PowerToys PR.
The next discriminator is comparing launch entry points and foreground-event ordering, not collecting another generic diagnostic archive.

reproduce.title: Non-dimming UAC focus ownership
reproduce.version_requirement: Compare a current supported build on Windows 11 with the historical maintainer reproduction.
prerequisites: Disposable test machine or VM; record and restore the original UAC setting
Use the consent-prompt setting that does not dim the desktop, not Never notify
Use a harmless known application requiring elevation; Run initially non-elevated.
steps: 1. Record the original UAC configuration and set the non-dimming consent option for this test only.
2. Activate Run, find the test application and press Ctrl+Shift+Enter; record foreground-window events and whether keyboard navigation reaches consent.
3. Cancel the prompt, then launch the same application elevated from Start and the taskbar under the same setting.
4. Compare Run hide/focus ordering and repeat with normal secure-desktop consent; restore the original UAC configuration afterward.
reproduce.expected_result: Determine whether Run uniquely retains focus or the same Windows limitation occurs across entry points, without bypassing consent.

actions.label: Review conditional elevation-handoff plan
actions.note: No security-policy change or consent-window manipulation is proposed; establish Run-specific ownership first.
